title: Canonical maps and equations in the geometric/residue-triple comparison
statement: Let A be a local commutative ring, K an extension field of its residue field and Omega an algebraically closed extension of K. The base residue map is the composite A -> k -> K, its residue point is the prime and residue embedding associated to Spec K -> Spec A, and its geometric point is Spec Omega -> Spec A induced by the composite. For an affine pointed etale neighbourhood n define its chart map A -> Gamma(n) by inverse GammaSpec followed by the structural map on global sections, and its evaluation Gamma(n) -> Omega by the lifted point on global sections followed by GammaSpec. For a residue triple t=(B,alpha,q,phi), define its residue map B -> K by inverse GammaSpec followed by evaluation at q and phi. A ring equality t.B=Gamma(n) represents n when it identifies the structural maps and, after embedding K in Omega, the residue map with the evaluation. For a small representative functor r and a residue-triple cocone c, a map g from its vertex to the geometric colimit satisfies coprojection compatibility when every represented pair (r(j),t) has c.ι(t) followed by g equal to the geometric coprojection at j, transported by that ring equality. These are the original eight comparison definitions, relocated verbatim into a module both lower comparison statements can import.
